top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a new class of matter: the time-reversal-invariant Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall state (Kane and Mele), with its first clean experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells (Molenkamp). It is distinct from the 2016 prize, which concerned topological invariants in one-dimensional chains and in the integer quantum Hall effect with broken time reversal. It is mature after about two decades of independent confirmation, and its consequences reach well beyond one subfield. The citation can be limited to the 2D discovery so it does not decide the contested 3D priority question, at the openly acknowledged cost of leaving out Hasan and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang. P002 is a mature, cleanly attributed prize that I rank second because I cannot test the metrology case directly and its distinctness from the 2005 and 2012 prizes is argued mainly by one member. No award is the weakest option because two sound, mature discoveries are available.
